questions.text: What is the register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: ENABLE 0x00 RW, PERIOD_REQ 0x04 RW reset 100, PERIOD_EFF 0x08 RO, STATUS 0x0C RO, FRAME_TOTAL 0x10 RO, OVERRUN_TOTAL 0x14 RO, COUNTER 0x18 RO, TAKE 0x1C WO, TICK 0x20 WO, all 32-bit
questions.reason: The request names registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping
STAT: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: [0] a frame waits, [1] enabled
OVERRUNS: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames dropped because one was waiting, wrapping
REQ: offset 0x01, RW, reset 100: [15:0] period asked for, as written
TICK: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks, one per clock; reads 0
CTRL: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [0] enable
CNT: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [15:0] ticks counted towards the next frame
TAKE: offset 0x04, WO, reset 0: any write takes the waiting frame; reads 0
EFF: offset 0x02, RO, reset 100: [15:0] period in force
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: unlisted offsets: read 0, writes dropped; read-only registers also drop writes
questions.evidence: FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping

questions.text: Does the PERIOD_EFF read show the period latched for the count in progress, or max(requested, PERIOD_MIN) now?
questions.default: The value latched for the count in progress (the period actually in force).
questions.reason: The request says a new request does not disturb the count, so the in-force value changes only at a wrap or enable.
questions.answer: Yes. The EFF register (the spec's name for the question's PERIOD_EFF) reads the period in force, which is the value latched for the count in progress. A new request does not change it until the next count or a switch-on, so it does not show max(requested, PERIOD_MIN) immediately. Note that the spec names the register EFF at offset 0x02, not PERIOD_EFF.
questions.evidence: EFF: offset 0x02, RO, reset 100: [15:0] period in force

questions.text: When a frame falls due in the same clock as a TAKE, what happens?
questions.default: The old frame is taken and the new one is held, with no overrun.
questions.reason: The take empties the slot before the new frame needs it.
questions.answer: The old frame is taken and the new one is held, with no overrun.

questions.text: Does an enable write of 1 while already 1 restart the count?
questions.default: No, only a 0 to 1 change restarts.
questions.reason: The request says switching on starts counting.
questions.answer: No. Writing 1 while enable is already 1 does nothing, so it does not restart the count. Only a 0-to-1 switch-on clears CNT and reloads EFF from the request.
questions.evidence: Switch-on (0 to 1) clears CNT and loads EFF from the request; switch-off clears CNT and the waiting frame; totals persist until reset; writing 1 while on does nothing.

questions.text: Where is the design ID TLP1 read, and what values do CLKS_PER_BIT and TIMEOUT_CYCLES take?
questions.default: ID is provided by the shell ID register, CLKS_PER_BIT 868, TIMEOUT_CYCLES 1000000.
questions.reason: Values are not given in the request.
questions.answer: The spec does not say where the design ID is read. The only design ID it gives is design_id 1414287409, not "TLP1", and the register map has no ID register, so the proposed shell ID register is not in the spec. CLKS_PER_BIT is 868. TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not 1000000 as proposed.
